title: 3. Circular Flow of Income, Factor Payments & Leakages

blocks.title: First-Principles Core Truth
blocks.summary: Income flows continuously between economic sectors through real factor/goods flows and counter-balancing monetary payments, governed by the identity of injections and leakages.

blocks.content: 1. Two-Sector Model (Households & Firms): Households supply factor services (Land, Labor, Capital, Entrepreneurship) and receive factor payments (Rent, Wages, Interest, Profit).
2. Real Flow vs. Money Flow: Real Flow is the physical movement of factor services and final goods. Money Flow is the opposite monetary payment for goods and factor services.
3. Leakages (Withdrawals): Income generated that is NOT spent on domestic consumption: Savings ($S$) + Taxes ($T$) + Imports ($M$).
4. Injections (Additions): Exogenous spending added into circular flow: Investment ($I$) + Government Expenditure ($G$) + Exports ($X$).

blocks.text:
⚡ 1. Real Flow vs. Money Flow Matrix
| Parameter | Real Flow (Physical Flow) | Money Flow (Nominal Flow) |
|---|---|---|
| **Definition** | Flow of factor services from households to firms, and final goods/services from firms to households | Flow of factor payments from firms to households, and consumption expenditure from households to firms |
| **Medium of Exchange** | Physical goods, services, and labor hours | Currency notes, bank deposits, and monetary assets |
| **Alternative Name** | Product / Factor Flow | Income / Expenditure Flow |

blocks.content:
#### A. Three-Sector Model (Households, Firms, Government)
- Government collects Taxes ($T$) from households/firms (Leakage).
- Government makes Transfer Payments & purchases goods/services ($G$) (Injection).

#### B. Four-Sector Model (Open Economy)
- Rest of World section adds Exports ($X$ - Injection) and Imports ($M$ - Leakage).

$$\text{Macroeconomic Equilibrium Condition: } \mathbf{\text{Total Leakages} = \text{Total Injections}}$$
$$\mathbf{S + T + M = I + G + X}$$

blocks.text:
🏛️ 3. Factor Income vs. Transfer Income
- **Factor Income:** Earnings received for rendering productive factor services (Rent, Wages, Interest, Profit). **INCLUDED in National Income!**
- **Transfer Income:** Money received without rendering any productive service in return (Unemployment allowance, Old-age pensions, Gifts, Pocket money). **EXCLUDED from National Income!**

⚖️ 4. Common Prelims & Mains Traps
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 1:** Old-age pensions are Transfer Income (EXCLUDED from National Income), but **Retirement Pensions** paid to retired employees are deferred factor payments for past services (INCLUDED in National Income!).
- ⚠️ **Exam Trap 2:** If Leakages exceed Injections ($S+T+M > I+G+X$), National Income ($GDP$) will **contract** in the next cycle until equilibrium is restored.

blocks.content:
#### Tier 1 — Recall MCQ
**Q:** Which of the following is classified as a 'Leakage' (Withdrawal) from the circular flow of income in a four-sector open economy?  
(A) Investment Expenditure ($I$)  
(B) Government Spending ($G$)  
(C) Imports ($M$)  
(D) Exports ($X$)  
**Answer:** ** — Imports represent money flowing out of domestic circular stream to foreign producers.

#### Tier 2 — Applied Scenario
**Scenario:** In an economy, private savings $S = ₹200	ext{ Cr}$, net taxes $T = ₹150	ext{ Cr}$, imports $M = ₹100	ext{ Cr}$, private investment $I = ₹250	ext{ Cr}$, and government expenditure $G = ₹100	ext{ Cr}$. What level of Exports ($X$) is required for circular flow equilibrium?  
**Resolution:** Equilibrium identity: $S + T + M = I + G + X implies 200 + 150 + 100 = 250 + 100 + X implies 450 = 350 + X implies mathbf{X = ₹100	ext{ Cr}}$.

#### Tier 3 — Mains Descriptive Prompt
*'Explain the mechanics of circular flow of income in an open economy. Differentiate between Factor Payments and Transfer Payments with suitable national accounting examples.'*
